newsitem.title: KENYA: KLM see continuing E.Africa cargo growth.
newsitem.headline: KLM see continuing E.Africa cargo growth.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines has seen "tremendous growth" in the air cargo industry in Kenya over the past few years and sees continued growth opportunities in Eastern Africa, a regional KLM manager said on Tuesday.
"Cargo is one of the growth areas in Kenya, it has grown tremendously in the past few years," said Wim ter Beek, general manager for Eastern Africa for KLM.

"Cargo is doing very well, there is a distinct local market here. You constantly see a lot of freighters, including Boeing 747s, at the Nairobi airport and there are at least 30 freighters going to Amsterdam each week. Martinair is here every day," he told Reuters in an interview.

Much of the air cargo exported out of Kenya was seasonal but the Kenyan airfreight market had matured considerably and the balance of inbound and outbound cargo was more equal today than ten years ago, he added.
KLM had flown between 60,000 and 70,000 passengers in 1996 and a total of 4,350 tonnes of cargo from East Africa, the majority of which was fresh fruits, vegetables, flowers and fish exports.
Imports mostly consisted of spare parts, foodstuffs, machinery, electronic goods and pharmaceuticals.
Cargo makes up some 30 percent of KLM's total business, ter Beek said, but declined to give exact figures on commercial grounds.
KLM was unlikely to increase cargo loads on its own flights due to its more lucrative passenger business. Next month flights between Nairobi and Amsterdam will be doubled, he said.

"We have three flights between Amsterdam and Nairobi but from the first of April we will introduce another three flights so we'll have a total of six fligths a week which will be run on a joint basis with Kenya Airways.
"We are confident that we can fill the capacity on all these flights," ter Beek said.
KLM bought a 26 percent share in Kenya Airways when the carrier was privatised one year ago, and results have to date been reported to be good.

Ter Beek said KLM -- through this new partnership -- was in the process of expanding into both existing and new markets in East Africa, with Tanzania and Uganda currently ranking second and third respectively.
"We are just starting to build up now. Tanzania is developing very well but the other markets in the region are also starting to come up now.
"Now we have to focus attention on Uganda which looks promising and even Eastern Zaire, Burundi and Rwanda are markets we plan to enter through Kenya Airways, using Nairobi as the air hub," he said.

Another notable change, he said, was that Kenya's tourism market had started picking up again after the year-low seasons of 1993 and 1994 which followed a rapid increase in crime and violent attacks on tourists.

"Since Christmas all our flights have been pretty full. The market is now picking up again and definitively, in the coming years, we will see a positive growth trend of between three and five percent".
"There is also a very constant increase in the number of routes to and from the Middle East, in particular Dubai," said ter Beek.
